newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian gas industry wants national market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian gas industry wants national market.

text.p: Australia's peak national gas industry organisation on Sunday urged the federal government to speed up the appointment of a national regulator and move quickly to create a national gas market.

"We (the industry) are saying it is time the federal government engaged us directly on these issues. There are issues we've had no consultation on whatsoever," Australian Gas Association (AGA) chairman Greg Harvey told a news conference at the start of a three-day AGA gas convention.
"The country has to develop an interstate market. To have a proper market, you can't have state markets," Harvey said.
"(But) we cannot commit the gas industry to decisions while there are grey areas," he said.
"Who is the identity of the government regulator? How much discretion is he going to have?" Harvey said.
He said the AGA wanted a national market based on commercial considerations but feared the government was formulating its plans on a consumer basis only.
"I believe there is a considerable danger we are moving from market-oriented to a consumer-basis market," Harvey said.
"It has got to be be a (government-industry) partnership but the last thing you need are labrynths of regulation," he said.

Harvey also released the latest industry statistics report for the year ended June 30, 1996 which showed natural gas had increased its primary energy share in Australia to 18.3 percent from 16.6 percent in 1994/95.
Total domestic sales of natural gas were up eight percent to 701 petajoules while natural gas production increased three percent to 1,216 petajoules in 1995/96.
Australia's current natural gas reserves, excluding coal seam methane, were estimated at 99,715 petajoules, enough for 89 years at current production levels, Harvey said.
